Q: When should you choose retrieval, a larger prompt or finetuning for a changing knowledge task?
spoken: Separate the defect first. Retrieval supplies changing external facts with source identity; context design selects what is exposed to the model; finetuning changes learned behavior from data. Evaluate a simple baseline and choose an intervention tied to observed errors. Finetuning does not by itself guarantee current facts, permission checks or supported citations.

Separate the defect first. Retrieval supplies changing external facts with source identity; context design selects what is exposed to the model; finetuning changes learned behavior from data. Concrete engineering case: A model answers correctly in a static benchmark but misses a policy updated yesterday. Training a larger adapter does not resolve the missing current source path.

Boundary defense: Investigate instructions, runtime schema handling and model capability on that slice. The appropriate repair can be different from adding more documents.
